title: 金庫が空っぽだ  (The Safe Is Empty)

segments.t: Just one morning after celebrating his number-one trophy, Muranishi arrives at Bianca International to find police officers outside the building. Inside, his section chief points to the open metal safe: Ono has vanished with every yen of the company's money. Listen to everything come crashing down.
英語の百科事典の会社だってさ。
最近はやってるみたいだな。
ああ、そうみたいだな。
課長、何かあったんですか？
大ありだよ。
会社の売上金が全部金庫から消えたんだよ。
えっ、全部ですか？
ほら、空っぽだよ。
小野さんはどこですか？
どこにもいないよ。会社は終わりだ。
そんな、信じられません。
今日はもう帰ります。
In twelve short lines, Muranishi goes from top salesman to unemployed. Let's look closely at the words that tell the story.
英語の百科事典の会社だってさ。

'They say it is an English encyclopedia company.' Native Japanese calls an encyclopedia "hyakka jiten", literally a 'hundred-subjects word-book'. Ending with "datte sa" passes along gossip—'so I hear'.
最近はやってるみたいだな。
'Looks like that business is popular lately.' "Hayatteru" comes from "hayaru", to be trendy or booming, and "mitai" adds 'it seems like'.
課長、何かあったんですか？
'Chief, did something happen?' Walk into any noisy crowd or office commotion and ask "nanika atta n desu ka", built from "nanika", something, plus "atta", happened.
大ありだよ。
'Something huge happened.' When someone asks if anything is wrong, "ooari", literally 'big-exists!', answers 'you bet there is—big time!'
会社の売上金が全部金庫から消えたんだよ。
'All the company sales money disappeared from the safe.' "Kaisha" is company, "zenbu" means all of it, "kinko" is a locked safe, and "kieta" comes from "kieru", to vanish.
ほら、空っぽだよ。
'Look, it is completely empty.' "Karappo" has a lively, hollow bounce to its sound and means completely empty—empty safe, empty box, or empty stomach.
小野さんはどこですか？
'Where is Ono-san?' Put anyone's name before "doko", where, and polite "desu ka" to ask where they are.
どこにもいないよ。
'He is nowhere to be found.' Pairing "doko ni mo" with negative "inai" sweeps every place clean: 'not anywhere at all'.
会社は終わりだ。
'The company is finished.' "Owari" turns "owaru", to end, into 'the end'—heard at closing time and when a venture goes under.
今日はもう帰ります。
'I am going home early today.' "Kaerimasu" is the polite everyday word for heading home—leading straight into Muranishi's early return to his house. Now let's listen to the office safe scene again.
英語の百科事典の会社だってさ。
最近はやってるみたいだな。
ああ、そうみたいだな。
課長、何かあったんですか？
大ありだよ。
会社の売上金が全部金庫から消えたんだよ。
えっ、全部ですか？
ほら、空っぽだよ。
小野さんはどこですか？
どこにもいないよ。会社は終わりだ。
そんな、信じられません。
今日はもう帰ります。
Hold on to "nanika atta n desu ka" to ask if something happened, "zenbu" for 'all of it', and "karappo" when something is completely empty. See you in the next scene.
さようなら。
